req.title: Retrieve all players
req.statement: The system shall respond to GET /players with a JSON array of all players in the database.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates GET /players/ returns HTTP 200 with a JSON array of all Player objects. I design: (1) a positive EP test asserting exact count (26 rows), status code 200, Content-Type, and spot-checking known field values from the seeded data; (2) a negative NEG test verifying that an unsupported HTTP method (POST with no body / wrong method) returns a client-error status, and that a malformed path returns 404 not 200; (3) a BVA boundary test asserting the exact array length equals 26 (the seeded row count), checking the first and last squad numbers present, and verifying the response is a list not a dict. Additional tests cover: cache header presence (X-Cache), response schema shape for every required field in PlayerResponseModel, and that the array is non-empty with exact length to catch off-by-one mutations on the DB query.

tests.name: test_get_all_players_returns_200_and_json_array
preconditions: Database is pre-loaded with exactly 26 player rows
FastAPI app is running in-process via TestClient
expected: Response body is a JSON array
Each element contains keys: id, firstName, lastName, squadNumber, position
trace: R-PLAYER-001: system shall respond to GET /players with a JSON array of all players
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_get_all_players_returns_200_and_json_array():
    r = client.get('/players/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert 'application/json' in r.headers['content-type']
    body = r.json()
    assert isinstance(body, list)
    assert len(body) == 26
    required_keys = {'id', 'firstName', 'lastName', 'squadNumber', 'position'}
    for player in body:
        assert required_keys.issubset(player.keys())

from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_get_all_players_exact_count_and_known_records():
    r = client.get('/players/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert isinstance(body, list)
    assert len(body) == 26
    squad_numbers = {p['squadNumber'] for p in body}
    assert squad_numbers == set(range(1, 27))
    by_squad = {p['squadNumber']: p for p in body}
    assert by_squad[1]['firstName'] == 'Anjali'
    assert by_squad[1]['lastName'] == 'Banerjee'
    assert by_squad[26]['firstName'] == 'Aditya'
    assert by_squad[26]['lastName'] == 'Mehta'

preconditions: Database seeded with exactly 26 rows — boundary value for array length
expected: len(body) == 26 exactly — catches off-by-one mutations on DB query or slice
trace: R-PLAYER-001: all players in the database; BVA on collection size
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_get_all_players_boundary_exact_26_rows():
    r = client.get('/players/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert isinstance(body, list)
    count = len(body)
    assert count == 26
    assert count != 25
    assert count != 27
    squad_numbers = sorted(p['squadNumber'] for p in body)
    assert squad_numbers[0] == 1
    assert squad_numbers[-1] == 26
    assert squad_numbers[12] == 13

tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_get_all_players_cache_header_present():
    r1 = client.get('/players/')
    assert r1.status_code == 200
    assert r1.headers.get('x-cache') == 'MISS'
    body1 = r1.json()
    assert isinstance(body1, list)
    assert len(body1) == 26
    r2 = client.get('/players/')
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    assert r2.headers.get('x-cache') == 'HIT'
    body2 = r2.json()
    assert isinstance(body2, list)
    assert len(body2) == 26

tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_get_all_players_spot_check_multiple_known_rows():
    r = client.get('/players/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert len(body) == 26
    by_squad = {p['squadNumber']: p for p in body}
    p3 = by_squad[3]
    assert p3['firstName'] == 'Kabir'
    assert p3['middleName'] == 'Karan'
    assert p3['lastName'] == 'Khan'
    assert p3['starting11'] is True
    p10 = by_squad[10]
    assert p10['firstName'] == 'Kabir'
    assert p10['middleName'] == 'Mary'
    assert p10['lastName'] == 'Reddy'
    assert p10['position'] == 'Right Winger'
    p15 = by_squad[15]
    assert p15['team'] == 'Chelsea'
    assert p15['league'] == 'Premier League'
    p25 = by_squad[25]
    assert p25['firstName'] == 'Lakshmi'
    assert p25['lastName'] == 'Saxena'
